data.narrative:
Astroscale, a public-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Mitsunobu Okada, has raised over $400M and currently trades at $840M. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 5 public and 8 private peers in space technology, including Rocket Lab, Planet Labs, and Firefly Aerospace.

The peer-median method provides the primary valuation anchor. Three same-sector, public-stage comparables—Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), and Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B)—yield a median valuation of $7.6B, with a range spanning $2.9B to $40.0B. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in business models and maturity within commercial space. Public-comp anchoring using sector price-to-sales multiples (median 27.4x across 6 Space & Aerospace tickers) is not applicable here due to the absence of disclosed revenue data.

The triangulated valuation range is $6.4B to $8.7B, centered at $7.6B. This implies Astroscale trades at a substantial discount to peer median—approximately 11% below—despite comparable stage and sector positioning. Key uncertainties include the wide spread in comparable valuations, limited applicability of revenue multiples, and the early-stage cash-generation profile typical in deep-tech space ventures. Sensitivity to near-term contract awards and technology milestone achievement remains material to valuation sustainability within the indicated range.
